title: Qhapaq Ñan, the Andean Road System
summary: The Qhapaq Ñan was the road network of the Inca state, running from Cusco to the four regions of Tawantinsuyu to move goods, people and messages. Built on earlier Andean roads from about 1000 BCE, it was expanded in the Inca expansion of 1493 to 1527 per ASCE. Six countries won joint UNESCO listing in 2014.

uncertainty.note: ASCE dates construction from 1000 BC (Chavin-period precursors) through 1533 AD, with Inca expansion under Pachacuti, Tupac Inka Yupanqui and Huayna Capac in 1493-1527 per the same page. The 2014 UNESCO listing is a later designation.
